title: O Holy Father! 'Mid the Calm
description: O Holy Father! 'Mid the Calm in Tonic Solfa to SWEET HOUR, doh is Db: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: William Henry Burleigh wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 26, “Evening Worship”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre Double (8.8.8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SWEET HOUR; any other Long Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Ho-ly Fa-ther! 'mid the calm And still-ness of_ this eve-ning hour, We would lift up our sol-emn psalm To praise Thy good_-ness, and Thy power For o-ver us, and o-ver all, Thy ten-der mer-cies still ex-tend, Nor vain-ly shall Thy child-ren call On Thee, our Fa_-ther and our Friend!

lines: And stillness of this evening hour,
We would lift up our solemn psalm
To praise Thy goodness, and Thy power
For over us, and over all,
Nor vainly shall Thy children call
On Thee, our Father and our Friend!
Kept by Thy goodness though the day,
Thanksgiving to Thy name we pour;
Night o'er us, with its stars, — we pray
Thy love, to guard us evermore!
In grief, console; in gladness, bless;
In darkness, guide; in sickness, cheer;
Before Thy throne our souls appear!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Henry Burleigh died in 1871.
credits: Words by William Henry Burleigh (1812–1871), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to SWEET HOUR by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
